subject: wearing flip-flops every day
title: What If You Always Wore Flip-Flops?

scenes.text: What if you wore flip-flops every day? Your toes would quietly take on a second job.
In an Auburn University test, thirty-nine students in flip-flops took shorter steps than in sneakers.
Their toes stayed curled, gripping to keep the sandal on, so the front of each foot lifted less with every swing.
Your clearance shrinks too. In one study, toes cleared the ground by about four centimeters barefoot, but flip-flops by under two.
Your heel also lands about twice as fast as barefoot, and your shin muscle works harder every step.
The Auburn team linked that walk to soreness from the feet up to the hips and lower back. The simplest shoe, the hardest-working feet.

description:
What if you always wore flip-flops? An Auburn University study of 39 college students found people took shorter steps in thong-style flip-flops than in athletic shoes and lifted their toes less, apparently gripping to hold the sandal on; the researchers linked the altered gait to sore feet, legs, hips and lower back.
A 2016 gait study (Irish Journal of Medical Science) found minimum toe clearance of 4.2 cm barefoot versus 1.6 cm for the flip-flop, and a 2014 Journal of Foot and Ankle Research study found heel contact velocity roughly doubled and more shin-muscle (tibialis anterior) activity compared with barefoot walking.
